strengths: The paper presents an original, practically useful approach to difficult three-view geometry. Centroid-based virtual correspondences allow four-point hypotheses to reuse established 5pt/6pt and P3P solvers. The deterministic construction is simple, and refinement on the original observations makes it attractive for integration into robust estimation pipelines.

The calibrated results substantiate a meaningful speed–accuracy trade-off. In Table 2, 4p3v(M±δ)+R+F achieves PhotoTourism AUC@10 of 70.47 at 75.78 ms, versus 70.54 at 105.50 ms for 5pt+P3P. The faster M+R+F variant also improves over HC [19] in both AUC@10 (69.06 versus 66.63) and runtime (30.54 versus 76.45 ms). These supported practical gains provide the main case for weak acceptance.

The evaluation is substantial: 5,000 triplets per scene across PhotoTourism and Cambridge Landmarks, two RANSAC frameworks, speed–accuracy curves, noise and outlier experiments, and refinement/filtering ablations. Parameters are validated on a held-out scene. Supplementary evaluation using all three camera pairs addresses a limitation of the main pose metric. The manuscript also candidly acknowledges approximation errors and the limited downstream benefit of learning.
weaknesses: The shared-focal-length extension has a weaker practical case. In Table 3, 4p3vf(M) achieves AUC@10 of 49.88 at 12.67 ms, versus 56.79 at 11.72 ms for 6pt+P3P. The best reported learned variant reaches only 53.56 while taking 259.63 ms. Using fewer observations remains valuable, but these results do not demonstrate a favorable accuracy–runtime trade-off against that baseline. Focal-length estimation errors are also not reported.

The geometric justification provides limited guidance about reliability. Lemma 1 bounds virtual-point error by triangle size; it does not establish small pose error or successful refinement. Figure 10 shows substantial errors even with noiseless observations, and Figure 14 documents unfavorable trade-offs on scenes such as Shop Facade and Trevi Fountain. The dependence on depth variation, viewing geometry, and triangle conditioning is not isolated, leaving the method's failure regimes incompletely characterized.

The learned component adds little demonstrated utility after refinement. On PhotoTourism, L+R has essentially the same AUC@10 as M+R (69.88 versus 69.90), but requires 297.88 versus 74.94 ms. Moreover, Equation (2) specifies a signed normalized epipolar residual rather than a nonnegative Sampson loss; minimizing it as written does not minimize geometric error. The actual training objective therefore needs clarification.

There are correctable reproducibility and reporting issues. Numerical RANSAC inlier thresholds are not specified. Section 4 states that the Nistér oracle performs worse than the proposed oracle, whereas supplementary Table 7 and Section 9.7 report the opposite after an insufficiently described RANSAC adjustment. These issues weaken experimental traceability, although they do not overturn the central calibrated results.
